svg.title: Cell processes
svg.desc: Chromosomes & genes: Nucleus contains DNA chromosomes, each with many genes; normally paired in body cells. After copying, each X is one chromosome with two joined identical copies (sister chromatids). Grow & copy DNA: Before mitosis: cell grows; more ribosomes and mitochondria form. DNA replicates. DNA amount doubles; chromosome number does not. Joined copies will separate. Mitosis: Joined copies separate; one complete set moves to each end. The nucleus divides. Copying happened before mitosis. Chromosome number is maintained, not halved. Divide the cell: Cytoplasm and membrane divide → two genetically identical daughter cells, with the parent’s chromosome number. For growth, development, repair/replacement, e.g. healing skin. Bacteria use binary fission, not mitosis. Human stem cells: Undifferentiated cells divide and produce cells that differentiate. Embryonic: most human types. Adult bone marrow: limited range, including blood cells. Source determines the range. Medical uses: Potential replacement of insulin-producing cells in diabetes, or nerve cells in paralysis. Therapeutic cloning: embryo has patient’s genes → matched tissue is not rejected by their immune system. Potential, not guaranteed cures. Benefits, risks & ethics: Benefit: repair damaged tissue. Risks: viral infection and uncontrolled division. Embryo destruction raises ethical/religious objections; others prioritise treatment benefits. Weigh source, benefits and risks; give a reasoned judgement. Plant meristems: Can form any plant cell type throughout life. Produce clones quickly and economically. Clone rare plants to prevent extinction; useful crops for features such as disease resistance. Plant cells come from plant meristems, not human stem cells.
